# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👌]

I can see the bomb’s complete visual state: display `0`, indicator light green, and five wires in order red, yellow, green, white, blue. I am sending these directly to Mute so the manual can determine the required action and relay it verbally to Blind. I cannot interpret the gestures as a code yet because no code has been established.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb view: display reads 0. Indicator light is green. Wires by position: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. Use the manual to determine the required action and tell Blind.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute has sent a victory-hand gesture, but no gesture code was established, so I cannot safely infer its meaning. I will ensure Blind has the visual facts and prompt Mute to communicate the manual’s exact instruction to Blind by speech.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Visual state unchanged: display 0, green light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. Mute should provide the manual's exact required action.")
speak(to="mute", text="I received your gesture, but we have no agreed gesture code. Please state the manual's exact required action aloud to Blind, including the target and any required setting.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb is still unchanged. Mute again signalled ✌, but that has no established meaning and cannot safely substitute for the manual’s instruction. I will again request that Mute speak the exact procedure to Blind; the visual wire data has already been supplied.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual's exact instruction to Blind now: identify whether to cut a wire, which wire by position and colour, or what other control to operate. Do not rely on gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb still shows the same state, and Mute continues sending ✌ without speaking. That gesture has no agreed meaning and cannot reach Blind, so no safe action has been identified. I will explicitly establish a visual prompt for Mute: 👋 means “speak the instruction aloud,” while also repeating the request in speech.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋"])
speak(to="mute", text="The gesture 👋 means: speak now. Blind cannot receive your gestures. Please say the manual's exact instruction aloud to Blind, including the wire position and colour or control to use.")
speak(to="blind", text="No safe action has yet been identified. Mute is being asked to state the manual's exact instruction aloud.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute has repeatedly shown ✌, which visibly represents two, but no code was agreed and I cannot safely know whether it means wire 2 or something else. I will relay the observation to Blind while emphasizing that it is not confirmed.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has repeatedly made the gesture ✌, visibly two raised fingers. This may indicate 2, possibly wire position 2, but no code was agreed, so treat it as unconfirmed. Bomb remains display 0, green light; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="Blind cannot see your ✌ gesture. If it means wire 2 or another action, say that exact instruction aloud to Blind.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute has sent ✌ on every turn, and the only concrete information this can safely convey is “two”; the likely manual-derived instruction is therefore to cut wire 2, which is yellow. I will tell Blind to cut the second/yellow wire. 

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's repeated ✌ indicates 2. Cut wire 2, the yellow wire.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[CUT] 3:[white] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous instruction was correct: wire 2 was cut, and the bomb has changed. The new visible state is display `0`, blue light, with wire 2 already cut; remaining wires are 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, and 5 red. I will send this state to Mute so the manual can determine the next action, and ask Mute to state it aloud for Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Correct change after cutting wire 2. New state: display 0, indicator light blue. Wire 2 is cut. Remaining wires: 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red. Consult the manual and state the exact next action aloud to Blind.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[CUT] 3:[white] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb is now at display `0` with a blue light. Wire 2 is already cut, and the remaining wires are 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, and 5 red. Mute has changed the repeated gesture from ✌ (“2”) to ☝ (“1”), strongly indicating wire 1. I will relay that wire 1, the green wire, should be cut.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's gesture ☝ indicates 1, following the established number pattern. Cut wire 1, the green wire.")
```
